title: Financial Quantitative Analysts
description: Develop quantitative techniques to inform securities investing, equities investing, pricing, or valuation of financial instruments. Develop mathematical or statistical models for risk management, asset optimization, pricing, or relative value analysis.

tasks.text: Apply mathematical or statistical techniques to address practical issues in finance, such as derivative valuation, securities trading, risk management, or financial market regulation.
Interpret results of financial analysis procedures.
Develop core analytical capabilities or model libraries, using advanced statistical, quantitative, or econometric techniques.
Maintain or modify all financial analytic models in use.
Devise or apply independent models or tools to help verify results of analytical systems.
Analyze pricing or risks of carbon trading products.

clusters.label: Drafting, Laying Out, and Specifying Technical Devices, Parts, and Equipment

tasks.text: Research or develop analytical tools to address issues such as portfolio construction or optimization, performance measurement, attribution, profit and loss measurement, or pricing models.
Collaborate in the development or testing of new analytical software to ensure compliance with user requirements, specifications, or scope.
Develop methods of assessing or measuring corporate performance in terms of environmental, social, and governance (ESG) issues.
Collaborate with product development teams to research, model, validate, or implement quantitative structured solutions for new or expanded markets.
Prepare requirements documentation for use by software developers.
Develop solutions to help clients hedge carbon exposure or risk.
Develop tools to assess green technologies or green financial products, such as green hedge funds or social responsibility investment funds.

clusters.label: Providing Consultation and Advice to Others

tasks.text: Define or recommend model specifications or data collection methods.
Provide application or analytical support to researchers or traders on issues such as valuations or data.

clusters.label: Communicating with Supervisors, Peers, or Subordinates

tasks.text: Confer with other financial engineers or analysts on trading strategies, market dynamics, or trading system performance to inform development of quantitative techniques.
Consult traders or other financial industry personnel to determine the need for new or improved analytical applications.

clusters.label: Judging the Qualities of Objects, Services, or People

tasks.text: Research new financial products or analytics to determine their usefulness.
Assess the potential impact of climate change on business financial issues, such as damage repairs, insurance costs, or potential disruptions of daily activities.
Produce written summary reports of financial research results.
Identify, track, or maintain metrics for trading system operations.

skills.name: Mathematics
skills.def: Using mathematics to solve problems.

skills.name: Critical Thinking
skills.def: Using logic and reasoning to identify the strengths and weaknesses of alternative solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems.

skills.name: Reading Comprehension
skills.def: Understanding written sentences and paragraphs in work-related documents.

skills.name: Complex Problem Solving
skills.def: Identifying complex problems and reviewing related information to develop and evaluate options and implement solutions.

skills.name: Active Listening
skills.def: Giving full attention to what other people are saying, taking time to understand the points being made, asking questions as appropriate, and not interrupting at inappropriate times.

skills.name: Speaking
skills.def: Talking to others to convey information effectively.

skills.name: Active Learning
skills.def: Understanding the implications of new information for both current and future problem-solving and decision-making.

skills.name: Judgment and Decision Making
skills.def: Considering the relative costs and benefits of potential actions to choose the most appropriate one.

skills.name: Writing
skills.def: Communicating effectively in writing as appropriate for the needs of the audience.

skills.name: Systems Analysis
skills.def: Determining how a system should work and how changes in conditions, operations, and the environment will affect outcomes.

skills.name: Systems Evaluation
skills.def: Identifying measures or indicators of system performance and the actions needed to improve or correct performance, relative to the goals of the system.

skills.name: Persuasion
skills.def: Persuading others to change their minds or behavior.

skills.name: Learning Strategies
skills.def: Selecting and using training/instructional methods and procedures appropriate for the situation when learning or teaching new things.

skills.name: Monitoring
skills.def: Monitoring/Assessing performance of yourself, other individuals, or organizations to make improvements or take corrective action.

skills.name: Social Perceptiveness
skills.def: Being aware of others' reactions and understanding why they react as they do.

skills.name: Coordination
skills.def: Adjusting actions in relation to others' actions.

skills.name: Instructing
skills.def: Teaching others how to do something.

skills.name: Time Management
skills.def: Managing one's own time and the time of others.

skills.name: Negotiation
skills.def: Bringing others together and trying to reconcile differences.

skills.name: Service Orientation
skills.def: Actively looking for ways to help people.

skills.name: Object or component oriented development software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications using object-oriented programming concepts. Examples: C#, C++, Oracle Java, Perl.

skills.name: Analytical or scientific software
skills.def: Software to capture data, perform analysis, or generate reports or visualizations to support scientific research. Examples: IBM SPSS Statistics, Insightful S-PLUS, SAS, StataCorp Stata.

skills.name: Data base user interface and query software
skills.def: Software to query, present, or edit information stored in a database sytem. Examples: Amazon Web Services AWS software, Microsoft Access, Microsoft SQL Server, Structured query language SQL.

skills.name: Development environment software
skills.def: Software to create or maintain applications which run on a computer or mobile device. Examples: Microsoft Azure software, Microsoft Visual Basic, Microsoft Visual Basic for Applications VBA, Microsoft Visual Studio.

skills.name: Business intelligence and data analysis software
skills.def: Software to present, visualize, or analyze data to help businesses make informed decisions. Examples: Microsoft Power BI, MicroStrategy, Tableau.

skills.name: Spreadsheet software
skills.def: Software to create or edit numbers or text organized into rows and columns of cells. May include formulas which recalculate values based on other cells. Examples: Microsoft Excel.
